questions: When fill_missing=True, does random filling apply only to columns that are numeric in the final DataFrame after initial construction (i.e., columns where all non-missing values are numeric), or does it also apply to columns that become numeric after random filling of some cells?
If a column is entirely missing (all NaN) and numeric, should random filling apply to all its cells when fill_missing=True?
Should the random integer range (num_range) be inclusive of both endpoints, as random.randint typically is?
If fill_missing=False, are missing values represented as NaN (float) or as None (object) in the resulting DataFrame?

When fill_missing=True, does the function fill missing values only in columns that are explicitly numeric (int64/float64) at the time of filling, or also in columns that could be interpreted as numeric but are currently object dtype due to mixed types?
If seed is provided, should the random number generator be reset for each column or each missing cell, or once globally?
Does the function handle the case where the number of provided columns is less than the maximum tuple length in the data?
Should the function raise an error if the data list contains non-tuple elements, or should it attempt to convert them?
